subject: Kickoff: OrionBionics marketplace commitment — sprint to signature & billing path
messages:
From: PrIyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@orionbionics.com>
Cc: Elena Rousseau <elena.rousseau@orionbionics.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Kickoff: OrionBionics marketplace commitment — sprint to signature & billing path

Alex / Elena — thanks again for the demo yesterday. As discussed, I put together a short mutual action sprint (attached) to get us from evaluation to committed private-offer on AWS. High-level asks and next steps below so we can align timelines this week: 

- Target goal: AWS Private Offer (Marketplace) to be active & first invoice flow validated by 2028-08-15.
- Key milestones: 1) Procurement asks collected (price structure, tax/KYC, legal redlines) — due 7/18; 2) Internal finance alignment on invoice method (Marketplace invoice vs direct invoicing) — due 7/22; 3) SOW + DocuSign executed — target 7/27; 4) AWS Private Offer creation + billing test — target 8/10.

Can you confirm:
1) Procurement contact and their preferred PO timeline (net 30 vs net 60)?
2) Whether you want Redwood to route invoicing via AWS Marketplace (we can upload invoice artifacts there) or have Redwood invoice OrionBionics directly (we'll need AP contact/email).
3) Any legal constraints (PO on file required prior to DocuSign, payment terms, or special tax handling)?

Attached: Kickoff-MAP-template.xlsx (worksheet with milestone checklist).

Thanks — I’ll loop in our finance and legal liaisons once you confirm the procurement path.

--
PrIyom Das
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
priyom@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0197
From: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@orionbionics.com>
To: PrIyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@orionbionics.com, Elena Rousseau <elena.rousseau@orionbionics.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Jul 2028 10:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Kickoff: OrionBionics marketplace commitment — sprint to signature & billing path

PrIyom — thanks for the summary and spreadsheet. Quick answers from procurement side: 

- We prefer AWS Marketplace Private Offer if Redwood can ensure the SKU/offer will appear under our account (preferred).
- Procurement requires a price breakdown (list price, committed discount table, expected monthly spend at tiers) and a tax/resale certificate note.
- Legal wants to see the SOW and standard T&Cs up front; they will typically require a PO to be raised before countersignature (~60 days lead time based on our current cadence).
- AP prefers Net 45; can do Net 30 if needed. Please send an AP contact to route invoices to.

Looping in Elena (IT procurement) — Elena, can you confirm if AWS Marketplace uploads are handled by your team or if we want Redwood to coordinate the upload to the private-offer listing?

On our side, target window looks like mid-August for go-live but our legal calendar is tight; if Redwood can accommodate a staged acceptance (technical sign-off first, commercial 1-2 weeks later) that would help.

Thanks,
Alex

From: PrIyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@orionbionics.com>, Elena Rousseau <elena.rousseau@orionbionics.com>, procurement@orionbionics.com
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Jul 2028 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Kickoff: OrionBionics marketplace commitment — sprint to signature & billing path

Thanks Alex — attached is an updated MAP that reflects the price tiers we discussed plus two billing options (Marketplace upload vs Redwood direct invoice). Also attached: draft SOW (Redwood standard) with the acceptance criteria we ran through in the POC.

Quick notes on the billing options (so internal and Orion folks have the tradeoffs):
- Option A — AWS Marketplace Private Offer: fastest way to get into Orion's procurement workflows; AWS issues the invoice to Orion and sends Redwood the settlement. Requires Redwood to prepare invoice artifacts and upload private-offer assets to AWS (we'll own that step). Advantage: aligns to your existing AP process and can be tied to the AWS account.
- Option B — Redwood direct invoice: Redwood issues monthly invoices to Orion's AP (PDF/email), we collect on our terms. Advantage: simpler for Redwood but may require additional vendor onboarding on Orion's side (W-9, tax forms) and could delay sign-off if procurement insists on marketplace flow.

Action items in the attached MAP (row-level owners):
- Procurement asks (Alex/Elena): confirm PO timing and AP contact by 7/20.
- Finance validation (Redwood - Naomi): confirm settlement routing for marketplace and expected lag by 7/22.
- Legal review (Jonas): quick pass on SOW redlines by 7/24.
- DocuSign + SOW: target ready for signature by 7/27.

Attachments: OrionBionics_MAP_v1.xlsx, SOW_Redwood_v2.pdf

Happy to hop on a 20-min call to walk through the MAP if helpful — propose 7/19 11am PT.

--
PrIyom Das
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: PrIyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, naomi_feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Jul 2028 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: OrionBionics MAP — decision needed on billing flow and discount table

Team — short internal thread to get alignment before I reply to Alex/Elena with our recommendation. Key points: 

1) Discounting / commit sizing: Orion indicated they want mid-tier commit (estimated $35k/month). I recommend we propose a 12-month commit at 20% discount with an overage rate to preserve margin. Thoughts?

2) Billing flow recommendation: Marketplace vs direct invoice. If we push Marketplace, we expect settlement lag (AWS payout ~30–45 days). Naomi, can you confirm expected cash lag and whether Redwood Finance can accept the 45-day settlement stretch on this account? If not, propose direct invoicing with Net 30 and a deposit/initial invoice to cover onboarding month.

3) Legal: Jonas, the SOW only has one small clause (data residency addendum) we expect Orion to request — can you give an estimated turnaround on a redline pass? 48 hours would be ideal.

I want to keep momentum — Alex asked for SOW + DocuSign ready 7/27. If we can't absorb a 45-day settlement gap, we'll recommend direct invoicing plus a 30% initial invoice to avoid cash flow risk. Please reply with approvals or objections by EOD 7/26.

Thanks — PrIyom
--
PrIyom Das
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Elena Rousseau <elena.rousseau@orionbionics.com>
To: PrIyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, naomi_feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Jul 2028 16:42:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Kickoff: OrionBionics marketplace commitment — sprint to signature & billing path

PrIyom / team — quick update from procurement & AP: 

- We reviewed the MAP and SOW; legal had one small redline that Jonas already accepted in the inline comments. Good to proceed.
- OrionBionics will sign via DocuSign today. PO has been raised: PO# ORB-2028-771. Procurement confirms Net 45 on the Marketplace settlement side.
- We prefer Redwood to upload the private-offer assets to AWS and coordinate the Marketplace listing under account ID 9876543210. Please confirm the AWS account ID you will target and the invoice artifact format AWS requires.
- DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.net/Member/PowerFormSigning.aspx?env=na1&token=abcdef123456 (signed copy will be routed to procurement@orionbionics.com).

Next steps for Redwood:
1) Confirm you will accept Marketplace settlement (Net 45) or request initial invoice — let us know by EOD 7/31.
2) Upload private-offer metadata and invoice artifacts to AWS and notify procurement when test invoice is ready.
3) Once DocuSign is complete, send final SOW copy and HubSpot record id so procurement can reconcile.

Thanks,
Elena Rousseau
Senior Procurement Manager | OrionBionics
procurement@orionbionics.com
